Event handler status missing after successful plan upgrade
After upgrading my plan, the subscription details page shows the payment as completed but the event handler section is blank. I expected to see the processing status confirming the webhook was handled successfully.

No event details shown for failed payments
When a payment intent is processing or has failed, the event history doesn't appear in the admin view. I expected to see the same tracking information that shows up once a payment succeeds.

Subscription type causes error when viewing account details
Attempting to view my subscription information triggers a server error after an upgrade. The system is unable to translate the stored subscription type into a readable format, which prevents the account details page from loading properly.

Webhook event status display crashes for certain records
When viewing the event handler details in the subscription dashboard, the page crashes with a server error for some webhook events. The issue occurs when the event's internal status doesn't match any of the predefined states. I expected the status to display as "unknown" or similar rather than causing a complete page failure.

Subscription status shows error instead of readable value
When viewing my subscription details, the status field throws an error rather than showing a human-readable label like created or completed. This happens when the subscription record contains a status value that doesn't match the expected options.

Immediate reload flag has no effect
When I start the development server with the immediate reload option enabled, connected browser clients don't reload automatically after the server starts. The server itself starts normally and all endpoints work, but the reload notification never reaches connected clients. I expect that with this option enabled, my open browser tabs should refresh automatically as soon as the server finishes initializing.

Help text implies port argument is optional
The runtornado command's help text wraps the address/port argument in square brackets, making it look like an optional parameter. In reality the argument is required and the command fails immediately if omitted.

Server won't start with IPv6 address
When I try to bind the server to an IPv6 address like [::1]:8000, it fails with an error saying the port is invalid even though I clearly provided one. Plain port numbers and IPv4 addresses work fine. I expected it to accept IPv6 addresses the same way.

Some image links bypass the proxy even though it's configured
When the image proxy is enabled, certain message images still display with direct external URLs instead of going through the proxy. This means third-party servers can see users' IP addresses when those images load, defeating the privacy protection. The issue appears consistently for specific types of links while others work fine.

Images fail to load through proxy after being sent
When I send a message with an image link, other users see the thumbnail but the image never loads through the caching proxy. The broken image icon persists even after refreshing the page. I expect all shared images to render normally via the proxy like they used to.

Error message omits the invalid queue ID
When subscribing to the real-time event stream, I receive an error saying my queue ID is bad, but the message never tells me which queue ID it found wrong. I have no way to know what needs to be fixed without checking server-side logs.

Error when digest email has no participants or channels
When I receive a digest email for a period where I had no activity, the email fails to render and shows an error instead of a clean "no new messages" state. The crash happens when the list of participants or channels being summarized is empty.

Macro includes silently ignored in certain documentation files
Macro include tags in some documentation pages appear as literal text instead of being expanded. The affected files should support macro includes, but the macro system is unexpectedly disabled for them, causing the raw macro syntax to show in the rendered output.

Can't remove emoji reaction after admin adds custom emoji with same name
I added a thumbsup reaction to a message using the standard emoji. Then our admin added a custom realm emoji also named "thumbsup". Now when I try to remove my reaction, it says the reaction doesn't exist even though I can see it on my message. If I don't specify the emoji type it always assumes the custom one instead of the standard emoji I actually used.

Adding a reaction with just the emoji name sometimes fails
When I click an emoji in the picker to react to a message, the reaction briefly appears then disappears. This happens most often after an admin has updated or deactivated a realm emoji. I expect the reaction to stay once I tap it.

Workplace users group check uses wrong organization's subgroups
When I try to delete or modify a user group, the system sometimes incorrectly blocks the action by claiming the group is part of my workplace users hierarchy. But the group isn't actually one of my organization's subgroups. It seems like the system is pulling subgroup data from another organization instead of just mine.

Workplace users group rejected despite having admin-only membership
When I try to set one of our existing user groups as the workplace users group, I get an error saying the group must be managed by organization administrators. The group I'm selecting is a regular group I created and all current members were manually added by admins. I expected to be able to use this group since its membership is fully under admin control.

Discounted pricing toggle hidden for $0 fixed-price plans
Our organization is on a cloud plan with a fixed price of zero due to a sponsorship agreement. We don't see the option to enable discounted pricing for non-workplace users in our billing settings, even though other organizations on similar plans can configure it. We expected to have the same option available since our effective price is already zero.

Scheduled email retries forever after a delivery failure
I noticed that a welcome email for a new user was never delivered, and the email delivery service was generating warning logs every 10 seconds for the same message. It seems that when an email cannot be delivered due to a permanent issue (like an invalid recipient address), the system keeps re-queuing and attempting the exact same message indefinitely instead of marking it as permanently failed or removing it from the queue.

Email delivery daemon stops after encountering a corrupted scheduled email
When a scheduled email entry has corrupted or invalid data, the entire email delivery process crashes and stops sending all queued messages. The problem persists until the service is manually restarted. I expected it to skip over bad entries and continue delivering other scheduled emails normally.

Data import upload fails without saving the file
When I upload a Slack data import during server setup, the upload process completes but then the uploaded file never appears as available for import. After refreshing the page, the import option is gone because the previously attempted upload isn't remembered.

File upload fails right after progress bar completes
On our S3-backed organization, file uploads sometimes fail right after the progress bar reaches 100%. The file doesn't appear in the chat after upload finishes, and I have to retry. I expected the file to be visible once the upload completed.

All uploads lose their original filenames
Every file I upload through the compose box shows up with a generic placeholder name instead of its actual filename. This happens for all files, whether images, documents, or archives.

Cancelled uploads leave orphaned files
I started uploading a large file but cancelled the upload partway through. The file still appeared in my uploads list and continued counting against our organization's storage quota, even though I never finished uploading it. I had to ask an administrator to manually remove the orphaned file from the system.

Analytics page crashes when no organizations exist
After deleting all organizations on my test server, the analytics section throws an error instead of showing an empty or gracefully degraded state. The system fails to load because it cannot compute a starting date for historical data when there are no organizations to reference.

Analytics data stops updating after upgrade
After upgrading the server, the analytics dashboard stopped showing new data. The last update date hasn't changed in days even though there's been plenty of activity. Restarting didn't help.

Slow loading of organization analytics
When I check the analytics dashboard for my organization, it takes a long time to load, particularly when looking at older time periods. Other sections that show per-user or per-channel breakdowns seem to load much faster.

Stream activity shows under wrong organization after move
I moved a channel to a new organization, but its message history and usage statistics still appear under the old organization in the analytics dashboard. The new organization shows zero activity for that channel even though people are actively using it. I expected the channel's historical counts to follow it to the new organization.

User activity stats shifted by one day
My analytics page shows my messages from Monday appearing under Tuesday, and today's row is empty. The total count is right, just the dates are off by one.

Avatar disappears when email has leading or trailing spaces
After my email was saved with a space at the end, my avatar image went blank while other users with the same base address still see theirs. I expected the system to strip whitespace before looking up the Gravatar match.

Avatar doesn't update after changing it
I uploaded a new profile picture but it still shows my old one even after waiting several minutes and hard-refreshing the browser. Other people in the same stream also see my old avatar. I expected my new picture to appear everywhere immediately.

LDAP profile picture changes after every directory sync
Our users' avatars appear to change randomly after each LDAP sync run, even though the actual images in our directory haven't been updated. The same photo is shown one day and then switches to a different-looking version the next.

Expected: If the LDAP directory hasn't changed, users should see the same avatar consistently across syncs.

Avatar images return 404 after server restart
After restarting the server, none of the user avatars load — every profile shows the default fallback icon. The issue persists across browsers and a hard refresh. It seems like the file lookup on disk fails for every user's avatar.

Bulk removal floods console with irrelevant messages
When I run the command with --all-users on a stream that only a few users were subscribed to, the output fills up with 'was not subscribed' lines for every other user in the organization. With hundreds of users this makes it nearly impossible to tell which users were actually removed.

User selection arguments missing from help output
When I run the command with --help, the output shows the stream and realm options but doesn't display any way to specify which users to remove. There's no mention of how to provide user emails or use the bulk removal option.

Return values table generated at wrong location when markdown has duplicate lines
When my documentation file contains two identical lines (for example, two consecutive blank lines or repeated section headers), the return values table gets inserted at the first occurrence instead of the intended one. I expected each template marker to be replaced at its own position in the file.

Description containing a colon is split into a field name and indented text
When I document an API response field whose description naturally contains a colon (for example, "Note: this field is only set when..."), the rendered documentation incorrectly treats the text before the colon as a field name. It displays "Note" with a type badge and pushes the rest of the sentence into indented body text below it, making the documentation confusing and hard to read.

API documentation indentation shifts left for union types
When viewing the return values table for an endpoint that uses a union type where some branches lack individual descriptions, the nested property fields appear indented too far to the left — they align with the parent field instead of being nested under their specific branch. This makes it hard to tell which properties belong to which branch of the union.

I was looking at the API reference page for an endpoint that returns a polymorphic response object. The first branch had a clear description, but subsequent branches had no per-branch description text. After those branches, all the child property lines were shifted left by four spaces compared to the branch with a description.

Events navigation table shows wrong operations
The sidebar navigation for events sometimes omits operation links or shows empty entries. I noticed this on the events documentation page — some event types that should show multiple operations (like "message" with both create and update) appear to have no operations listed at all, while others display correctly. Reloading the page doesn't fix it; the behavior seems to depend on how the page was generated.

Expected: All event types with operations should consistently show their operation links in the navigation table.

Map field with nested dynamic properties is incomplete
When I view the API documentation for a field that accepts both predefined properties and arbitrary additional key-value pairs, only the predefined properties are listed. The section that should describe the arbitrary additional fields is missing entirely, so I can't tell what other data the API might return.

Sponsorship request form rejects valid organization website URL
When I try to submit a sponsorship request for our community organization, the form won't accept our website URL even though it's a normal, complete address. The URL gets cut off or rejected before I can save the request. I expected to be able to enter our full organization website without the form limiting how much of it I can include.

Unspecified appears as a selectable plan option
When filling out a sponsorship request form, users see Unspecified listed alongside Community, Basic, and Business plans in the plan selection dropdown. They expected to only see actual plan options and were confused by this entry.

Error message is confusing when scrubbing an active realm
I ran the scrub command on a realm that was still active, and the error said "Please deactivate the realm the first." The phrasing is awkward and doesn't clearly tell me what to do next. I had to look up documentation to figure out I needed to deactivate the realm first.

Expected: A clear instruction like "Please deactivate the realm before scrubbing it."

No force flag for destructive scrub command
I ran the scrub command on a deactivated organization and it immediately wiped all data without asking for confirmation. For such a destructive operation I expected at least a --force flag to make it explicit, or an interactive prompt. Running the command with just the realm identifier feels too easy to trigger accidentally.

Emails fail to forward when they have no HTML version
When I enable email forwarding in development, some emails silently fail to send. This happens with notifications that only have plain-text content and no HTML alternative. The forwarding setup works fine for regular messages with HTML, but any email without an HTML body causes the entire send to fail.

I expected all emails to be forwarded regardless of whether they include HTML content.

Email log shows \"Missing HTML message\" placeholder
When viewing the development email log, some emails display \"Missing HTML message\" in the HTML content section even though the email has a valid plain-text body. I expected the log to show the email body or leave the section blank rather than showing this placeholder text.

Emails silently dropped when no forwarding address is configured
I enabled development email logging to inspect outgoing messages, but none of the emails actually get delivered anywhere. The send call returns a success count even though nothing was transmitted. I expected the emails to be sent through the normal SMTP channel when no forwarding address is configured.

Comments stripped from development email config when updating forwarding address
I added explanatory comments to the development email configuration file so my team could understand the settings. After using the admin panel to update the forwarding address, every comment I'd written was gone—the file was completely rewritten with only raw key-value pairs.

Email forwarding silently disabled after config file reset
I configured email forwarding in my development environment by setting the forward address, but newly sent emails were delivered to the original recipients instead of being forwarded. The configuration file had been cleared between sessions, and the system fell back to normal delivery without any warning or error message.

Search index audit locks the entire messages table
Running the search index audit command blocks all message writes for minutes. While it runs, users cannot send or receive messages — the app appears frozen. I expected it to process in smaller batches so the rest of the site stays responsive.

Link-type embeds silently fail
When I paste a URL that returns an oEmbed link type response, nothing shows up as a preview in the message composer. Other URLs from the same provider work fine when they return photo or video embeds. I expected all valid oEmbed responses to display a preview card with the title and URL.

Link preview shows wrong embed type
When I paste a URL that has both oembed and open graph metadata, the resulting link preview sometimes displays as a photo when it should be a video (or vice versa). The type information from one parser gets lost when the data is combined with the other parser's results. I expected the embed type to reflect the most complete metadata available across all sources.

Markdown diff tool crashes on output starting with a dash
When I run tests comparing rendered Markdown that begins with a dash character, the diff tool crashes with an argument parsing error instead of showing the comparison. I expected to see a normal diff highlighting the differences between actual and expected output. Tests work fine when the content doesn't start with a dash.

Unhelpful error when markdown diff tool is missing
When running tests without building the frontend first, I get an error saying it cannot find the markdown diff tool, but there is no hint about how to fix it. I expected the message to tell me to run the build step or install dependencies.

Steps: 1) Clean checkout without building assets. 2) Run tests that use markdown diff comparison. 3) See cryptic error with no actionable guidance.

Queue worker never restarts after database outage
When the database connection drops during event processing, the worker logs the error and saves the failed events to an error file, but it never automatically recovers even after the database comes back online. The worker remains stuck in a failed state until someone manually restarts the service.

Failed queue events disappear without retry
When an event fails during processing it gets logged and written to an error file, but the worker then moves on to the next event without ever re-queuing or retrying the failed one. The event is silently dropped.

Batch processing timeout multiplies by event count
I set a thirty-second timeout expecting it to cap how long the entire batch could take, but when ten events arrived together they were allowed to run for five minutes before timing out. The timeout scales with the number of events instead of applying once to the whole batch.

Messages fail after queue goes idle
When the queue empties and then receives new messages, the very first message always fails with a generic processing error. The message content is valid and succeeds on retry. The failure happens right as the worker wakes up from idle state.

Timeout error message shows inflated duration
When a queue worker times out while processing multiple events, the error message in the logs reports a much longer timeout than the configured limit—for example, claiming a 60-second timeout when only 30 seconds were set. The reported duration scales with the number of events being processed, making it hard to diagnose actual performance issues.

Link embeds missing for some URLs when a message contains multiple links
When I send a message with several links, only some of them display preview cards with titles and images. The ones that fail seem to come after the first problematic link in my message. I expected all valid links to show embeds regardless of whether other links had issues.

Link preview fetch appears to hang on messages with many URLs
When posting a message containing multiple links, the embedded link previews sometimes fail to load and remain blank. The issue seems to occur specifically when there are several URLs in a single message. I expected all link previews to appear after the message is posted.

Emoji status displays inconsistently across devices
When I set an emoji status using the status picker, it appears correctly right away, but after switching devices or refreshing, the emoji sometimes renders as a broken image or falls back to plain text. The status text and name are fine—only the emoji rendering is off. I expected my emoji status to look the same everywhere.

Message history shows lower count for today than expected
In the installation activity dashboard, the daily message count column for today consistently shows fewer messages than any of the previous seven days, even though usage has been steady. I checked the activity log and confirmed that there were plenty of messages sent this morning — the number just doesn't add up to what a full day should have.

I expected today's count to reflect a complete 24-hour period like the other days in the history row.

New users auto-subscribed to deactivated channels
When I deactivate a default channel and then create a new user account, that user is automatically subscribed to the deactivated channel. The channel should not appear in the subscription list for new users since it has been deactivated by an administrator.

Default channels from other organizations appearing in my workspace
Several channels marked as default in my organization are actually part of a different organization. They show up in my default channel list even though I have no business being there. This started after a recent data migration between workspaces.

Command crashes with unhandled error when LDAP user lacks email attribute
When I ran the LDAP query tool for a user whose directory entry is missing the configured email field, the command crashed with a traceback instead of showing a helpful error. I expected it to either display "email: LDAP field not present" like it does for other missing attributes, or at least show a clear message about the missing email attribute.

Angle brackets shown in argument help confuse usage
When I run the management command with --help, the email argument display includes literal angle brackets around the word email. This makes it unclear whether I should type the brackets as part of my input or just the email address itself.

Activity page times out for active users
When I view the activity page for a power user from the admin panel, the page takes over a minute to load or times out entirely. Other users' activity pages load instantly. I expected all activity pages to load within a few seconds regardless of how many records exist.

Server admin activity page loads extremely slowly for active users
When I open the activity page for a frequently-used account, the page takes over 30 seconds to load and sometimes times out. I was reviewing recent search activity for a power user who makes hundreds of queries daily. The page should render quickly regardless of how many activity records exist.

Download notifications missing when upgrade flag isn't in payload
Some episode downloads don't generate a message in the stream even though the download completed successfully. This happens when the webhook payload doesn't include the upgrade status field. I expected every download event to produce a notification regardless of whether it was an upgrade.

Webhook crashes when updating board description
When someone changes a board's description (not its name), the Trello webhook delivery fails and nothing posts to the stream. Renaming the board works fine, but any other board setting change causes the integration to error out entirely.

Notifications fail when webhook has no creator
Some Trello board actions don't generate notifications in Zulip. When the webhook payload doesn't include a member creator, the notification silently fails and nothing appears in the stream. I expected the message to post even without creator information.

Upgrade fails after paying invoice
After my team paid the invoice to upgrade our plan, the system crashed and the upgrade never went through. The payment was confirmed, but the transaction details were missing the license count and license management settings. I expected the upgrade to proceed using sensible defaults when those optional details weren't included.

Card update appears successful but card isn't saved
After completing the checkout flow to add a new payment method, the confirmation message shows success, but when I check my billing page, the card isn't there. I had to repeat the checkout process, and it worked the second time.

No email alert when invoice webhook crashes
When an invoice payment webhook fails due to an internal error like a database timeout, the billing team receives no email notification. The system only sends alerts for billing validation errors, so crashes and infrastructure issues go unnoticed until someone discovers a customer's plan wasn't upgraded.

Payment method update fails after organization merge
After our organizations were merged, updating my payment method on the billing page returns an error. Other billing operations work fine, but any attempt to add or change a card fails immediately.

Management command gives no feedback when user not found
I ran the email change management command to update a user's address, but I typed the old address wrong. Instead of a clear message saying the user wasn't found, the command just crashed with a raw traceback and no hint about what went wrong. I had to dig through the error to figure out I misspelled the email.

Command changes wrong user's email when realm not specified
I ran the management command to change a user's email on our multi-organization server without passing --realm. The command appeared to succeed, but it changed the email on a different user from another organization that happened to share the same email address. Other similar management commands require specifying the realm explicitly, but this one accepts it as optional.

Build failure notifications have awkward wording
When a build fails, the Zulip notification reads "has failed status" instead of a simple status word like "started" or "succeeded" used for other states. The message reads as "[Build](url) triggered by user on master branch has failed status." which is grammatically awkward and confusing compared to the clean phrasing for mapped statuses.

Authentication backend toggle reports success but changes don't take effect
I used the management command to enable a new authentication backend for our realm. The command printed "Done!" and showed the backend listed under enabled backends. When I tried logging in through that backend, authentication failed, and checking the realm settings later showed the backend was still disabled. The changes only appeared to take effect after restarting the server.

Cannot enable a new authentication backend
I tried to enable GitHub authentication for my realm using the management command, but it rejected the request saying GitHub is not a valid backend. The error only lists the backends already configured, so I can't tell which ones are available to enable. I expected the command to accept any supported backend type and add it to the configuration.

Authentication backends listed in random order
When I run the show command to see which authentication backends are enabled for my realm, the list order changes between runs even though nothing has changed. Sometimes GitHub appears first, sometimes LDAP, sometimes Google. I expected the backends to be listed in a consistent, alphabetical order so I can quickly scan the output.

Expected instead: a stable, predictable ordering of the backends in the displayed output.

Management command gives cryptic error when no action is specified
When I run the command to change authentication backends without providing --enable, --disable, or --show, I get a confusing Django argument parser error instead of a helpful message explaining what options are available.

Multiple reminder messages scheduled when opting to watch video later
When I mark the navigation tour video as read and choose to watch it later, the system schedules a reminder message. But if I do this twice (maybe I refresh or click back), I end up with two separate reminder messages waiting for me. I expected only one reminder to be scheduled regardless of how many times I make the choice.
